log.msg: ITEM 1 DONE, and the grep is the proof: `grep -rn "SURFACES\s*=" public/` returns ONE line, core/Page/words.js:138, where it returned three this morning. The five lists (navigation, width, arrangement, surfaces, type size) are core's; blocks.js IMPORTS and re-exports them under the realm's older names (ROOM = core's WIDTH, TYPE = core's TYPE_SIZE) so nine importers are untouched. One trap paid for: `export ... from` is a pass-through and does NOT bind the names locally, so CONTROLS below it would have thrown `NAVIGATION is not defined` on first import with every page in the realm blank - the file imports AND re-exports. system.js re-exports core's list and keeps only SURFACE_CLASS (its own paint); LayoutsCard reads `{id,title,means}` objects in three places instead of a string array plus a SURFACE_MEANS map. tone.js keeps four TONES and gains the comment that says surface IS card and wash IS tint.

ITEM 6, AND THE OWNER WAS LOOKING AT THE LAB, NOT AT ext/tabs. Measured before, at 1280 and 3440 on /imagine/paging/: the demo's own strip (.paging-strip, not ext/tabs) had ZERO tabs lit at rest (any_on 0), 9px of gap at 1280 and 28px at 3440 between the strip and the box, and a bordered rounded card under it. ext/tabs' own default tab WAS lit correctly on both heavy users I checked. So the fix is two: (a) the lab's strip gains a first tab for the page ITSELF - exactly what ext/tabs calls tab-default - lit at rest, and the frame's middle gap goes to 0 under the tabs word with the box's top corners squared; (b) the sitewide flip the owner asked for anyway - flush is the default, the bounded panel the 09-05 pass made default is now the opt-in `.tabs.bounded`, which nothing on the site says. After: gap 0 at both widths, one tab lit; on /framework/core/Page/ and /framework/ext/Doc/ the panel's border went 1px -> 0 and its fill rgb(242,242,242) -> transparent at 1280 and 3440, selected tab still lit. The panel's 3em top padding is untouched - it is the site's rhythm and predates the bounded pass.

ITEM 8, WITH THE NUMBERS. Before: the paging rail is 413px wide at 3440 inside a 3440px app row, and `--pad-ramp` is `clamp(1em, 2.6% - 1.1em, 4em)` - a PERCENTAGE, which resolves against the containing block - so it read 2.6% of 3440 minus 1.1em = 69.6px and put it on the rail: 33.7% of the rail spent on inset. After: 22.7px, 11.0%, 1.26em. At 1280 it goes 16.7px -> 13.2px. WHY NOT cqi, since the owner asked: an element is NEVER its own query container, so a box can only pad in cqi if the CONTAINER is an ancestor and the padding sits on something INSIDE it - the columns host's seam works because `.page.columns` is the container and `.page-column-item` is the padded thing. This rail declares its own width in a token, so a fraction of that token is the same intent with no extra element and no container-type (which would make the rail a containing block for every position:fixed inside it). Core's side boxes got the same treatment: `.page-rail/.page-panel/.page-aside` now name their width `--page-side-w` and derive `--pad` from it.

ITEM 7 PROVEN BY ui-test, nine steps (scratchpad g3-path2-out). At rest the path bar reads `/` and the Home tab is lit; picking Dashboard changes the ROOT's box. Clicking Overview: the path reads `/overview`, and the Content dropdown shows `dashboard` - because a child INHERITS the root's content word until you set one, which is the answer to `when you click Overview it's not the default content`. Picking Settings there changes OVERVIEW's panel. Clicking Home: the path is `/` again, the dropdown reads `dashboard` again, the root's box is still the dashboard (the child's edit did not touch it) and the address still says ?content=dashboard. The path bar is ext/demo's own `.demo-shell-path` - app.js already loads that sheet on every page - with one change: no separator and no gap, because `/ > overview` is not a path anybody would type.

ITEM 9: I applied the RULE rather than the count. Seven of nav-fat's ten are a gap INSIDE one control and are back in its own em - .page-column-item, .page-preview-link, .page-gen-item, the generator's list row and wall tile, the grid tile in grids.css, .page-uses-row. THREE are kept on the ramp with the reason written at the spot, because the rule's other half says so: .page-gen-export-row (a field beside a button - two sibling controls), the generator's tab strip gap (sibling tabs, the same call .demo-mini-tabs got) and grids.css's wall gap (between sibling tiles). Measured at 3440 on /imagine/: .page-column-item's icon-to-label gap was 16.84px on the ramp and is 6.48px now - 2.6x, exactly the cap arithmetic the addendum predicts.

ITEMS 2, 3, 4 AND 5 DONE. (2) Each arrangement value names the core/Layout it compiles to - plain/bar-top/bar-bottom -> stack, rail-left/rail-right -> rail-and-content, main-aside -> main-aside, wall -> wall - and the lab's control draws that link as a SIBLING of the value's card, because a card is one <a> and an <a> in an <a> is un-nested by the browser without a word. (3) The <34em stacking query is scoped: only a page's OWN frame is a container (`.page-frame-page`, stamped by render()), so a frame drawn as a picture has none to ask; the lab's `container-type: normal` patch is deleted and its full-size stage opts back in with one `:not()` rule. Proved: the six-word page stacks at 400 and not at 1280/1920/3440, the lab stage stacks at 400 (rail 316px = the whole row) and sits beside at 1280, and Cross's cells are unchanged. (4) tree.js is DELETED - `cap`, `facets` and `search` are options on browse() now, a facet reads a child page's prop straight, and the three older callers keep the same button classes, the same `Everything` label and no new rules (the one search-width rule is scoped `:has(.browse-facet-head)` so only a faceted rail gets it). Six now-dead selectors went from Layout.css. (5) core/Page/doc/words.md is one screen: the six words in a table, one page file before and after it says three words, then the layout tree and the lab. Registered in page.js `notes:` and `files:`, linked from readme.md.

ITEMS 10 AND 11 (the Section build's two core defects). Page.from() said `new Page(...)` and `Page.from(...)` in its recursion, so no subclass could inherit it - that is why core/Section carried an 18-line near-copy. It says `new this(...)` and `this.from(...)` now, and the keys moved into `static props(data, mode)` so a subclass ADDS its own instead of copying the reader. Section.from() is deleted; Section keeps six lines of props(). Proved live: Section.from('/framework/core/Section/example/') returns a Section with layout main-aside, editing false, 2 children, and the first child is a Section too. (11) A page whose `content` is a plain STRING returned a bare text node into `.page`, which is a grid - and `.page > *` cannot match a text node, so it became an anonymous item in the implicit first track (the gutter). `render_content()` wraps a string in p() now: measured after, 602x68px at 1280 and 344x105 at 400, in the reading track.

assign.outcome:
**One copy of every word list, the demo has an address, and the tabs are flush.** Eleven things, each measured.

![the paging demo: the path bar reads `/`, the Home tab is selected and joined to the box, the rail is no longer padding on the row's width](demo.png)

**The five word lists are core's.** [`core/Page/words.js`](/framework/core/Page/words.js) holds navigation, width, arrangement, the five surfaces and the three type steps. `grep -rn "SURFACES\s*=" public/` returned **three** definitions this morning and returns **one** now. Nine importers were not touched: the paging lab re-exports them under its older names, `/imagine/sections/` and `/imagine/layouts/` read core's, and `styles/sections/tone.js` gained the comment saying its `surface` IS `card` and its `wash` IS `tint`.

**Each arrangement word links to the layout it compiles to** - [the catalogue of thirty](/framework/core/Layout/), each proven at seven widths - drawn as a sibling of the value's card, because a card is one `<a>`.

**The `< 34em` stacking query is scoped, and the lab's patch is deleted.** Only a page's OWN frame is a container now (`.page-frame-page`), so a frame drawn as a *picture* of a page has none to ask. Proved: a page saying all six words stacks at 400 and not above; the lab's full-size stage opts back in with one rule and still stacks at 400 (rail 316px = the whole row); Cross's cells are unchanged.

**`core/Layout/tree.js` is gone.** `cap`, `facets` and `search` are options on [`browse()`](/framework/ext/catalog/doc/method/browse.md) - a facet reads a child page's prop straight, no schema. The three older walls ([core/Page](/framework/core/Page/), [styles/layouts](/framework/styles/layouts/), [ui](/framework/ui/)) were A/B'd against the old implementation loaded into the same live document: **character-identical HTML, 18,093 / 171,718 / 910 chars, at 1280 and 3440.**

**The owner's four findings, each at the cause**

- **The demo has an address.** A path bar reads `/` at rest and `/overview` after a click; the first tab is the page itself and is lit at rest; the `content` word edits the page at the current path and a child inherits the root's until you set one. Nine `ui-test` steps pass, and `?content=` still round-trips.
- **Tabs are flush.** The demo's strip had **9px at 1280 and 28px at 3440** between it and the box - now **0** at both, with the box's top corners squared. Sitewide, the 2026-09-05 bounded panel became the opt-in `.tabs.bounded` that nothing says: on [core/Page](/framework/core/Page/) and [ext/Doc](/framework/ext/Doc/) the panel's border went 1px to 0 and its fill to transparent, selected tab still lit.
- **The rail padded on the app row's width.** `--pad-ramp` is a *percentage*, so a 413px rail inside a 3440px row took **69.6px a side - 33.7% of the rail**. Now **22.7px, 11.0%, 1.26em**. `cqi` is unavailable here and the reason is worth keeping: an element is never its own query container, so `cqi` padding needs an inner box; a rail that declares its width in a token can pad off that token instead.
- **Ten ramp reads under `core/Page/**`.** Seven were a gap INSIDE one control and are back in its own em; three separate sibling controls and keep the ramp, with the reason at the spot. Measured at 3440: `.page-column-item`'s icon-to-label gap was **16.84px** and is **6.48px**.

**Two core defects the Section build found.** `Page.from()` said `new Page(...)`, so no subclass could inherit it - it says `new this(...)` and `this.from(...)` now, with the keys in `static props()`, and `core/Section`'s 18-line copy is deleted (`Section.from()` returns a Section, children included). And a page whose `content` is a plain string returned a bare text node into the page GRID, which `.page > *` cannot reach - it lands in the reading track as a paragraph now.

**The proof.** **787 loads** - all 631 pages of `core/Search`'s corpus at 1280, plus the paging, sections, layouts and core/Layout realms at 400/1280/1920/3440 - before and after. **Zero new console messages.** Four differences, all checked and none mine: two headless-GPU warnings on `/imagine/scenes/`, one timeout that swapped pages between runs (both load in 0.9s alone), and `/imagine/research/disclosure/`'s declared-child probe 404, which is deterministic and pre-existing.

**Left, with reasons.** The lab's rail and rows still light nothing when no child is open - the owner named tabs, and a rail beside a box reads as a list rather than a selector. `/imagine/layouts/`'s `LayoutsCard` and `number.js` were not deleted: `core/Layout` catalogues arrangements and that realm still teaches its numbered eighteen, so replacing one with the other is the owner's call, not a side effect of this slice.
